Access to Amazon and bank accounts
Fraudulent orders; bank account email changed

summary: In May 2026 attackers compromised town hall computers in the Town of Alexandria, Tennessee. City clerk Jessica Howard discovered unauthorized orders for three cameras and an iPad placed through the town's Amazon account (one camera charge of $748.18 was later refunded by the bank); the attackers also accessed the town's bank accounts and changed the email address on file, though no funds were stolen. Police are investigating with help from a New York investigator, and the town engaged IT vendor Winslow Enterprises to remediate.
